data.title: Israel's Netanyahu denounces enemies, allies in fiery UN speech
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, facing a difficult reelection campaign at home, delivered a fiery UN speech Thursday assailing enemies and allies alike -- and sparking uproar in the chamber.

data.title: Hollywood stars among arrests in NY anti-Netanyahu protest
data.description: NEW YORK - Movie star Susan Sarandon and "Hacks" actress Hannah Einbinder were among people detained by police in New York on Thursday as they moved in to break up a protest against Benjamin Netanyahu.

data.title: French actress Marina Vlady dies at 88
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French actress Marina Vlady, who appeared in more than 80 films and picked up a prize at the Cannes Film Festival in 1963, died on Thursday at the age of 88, her family told AFP.

data.title: Israel policies threaten 'life and existence' of Palestinians, Abbas says
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas said at the UN on Thursday that Israeli policies no longer just jeopardized a two-state solution but were now threatening the "very life and existence" of his people.

data.title: Eviction of pensioner puts Spain housing crisis in spotlight
data.description: MADRID — The eviction of an 87-year-old from her Madrid home has highlighted a political paralysis that has thwarted efforts to resolve Spain's chronic housing crisis, fuelling debate before next year's election.

data.title: UK man died putting women, children first in Mozambique jihadist siege
data.description: WINCHESTER — A British contractor trapped during a 2021 siege by jihadists in Mozambique was "unlawfully killed" after refusing to escape by helicopter, insisting women and children be evacuated first, a coroner ruled Thursday.

data.title: Israel's US envoy says son fighting for life
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israel's ambassador to the United States said Thursday that his soldier son was fighting for his life after a Palestinian attacker rammed his car into him at a checkpoint in the occupied West Bank.

data.title: 'I was drowning': Iran Nobel winner exposes pain of separation from children
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Iranian Nobel peace prize winner Narges Mohammadi has said her biggest fear is dying without seeing her two children again after being separated from the twins for over a decade, in her memoir published on Thursday.

data.title: Eight killed in wave of Russian strikes on Ukraine
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - A barrage of Russian drone and missile strikes pummelled Ukraine on Thursday, killing six agricultural workers in the east alongside two in the capital, Kyiv, the latest in an intensifying exchange of attacks.

data.title: Tigray rebels in ‘full-blown war’ with Ethiopian forces
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Tigray rebels in Ethiopia told AFP on Thursday they were in a state of “full-blown war” with the federal government, as heavy artillery attacks were reported in neighbouring states.

data.title: Mexican cartels target Australia with African meth
data.description: JOHANNESBURG - The Mexican “tourists” told immigration officers in Johannesburg they had come to see the “Big Five” of South Africa’s game parks — the elephants, rhinos, lions, leopards and buffaloes that draw millions every year.

data.title: Thailand slams ‘chaotic’ Asian Games organisation
data.description: NAGOYA, Japan - Thailand is the latest country to speak out about the organisation at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan, likening it to a “chaotic” game of “musical chairs”.

data.title: North Korea to keep nukes ‘forever’, says minister
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea will keep its nuclear weapons "forever", its foreign minister vowed on Thursday, dismissing the South Korean president's renewed calls for a denuclearised Korean Peninsula.

data.title: Pakistan strikes ‘terrorist sanctuaries’ in Afghanistan
data.description: An overnight airstrike hit the southern Afghan city of Kandahar, home to the Taliban government’s supreme leader, a resident told AFP early Thursday.

data.title: Catholic baptisms rise among French youth
data.description: MAUREPAS, France - Feeling a little nervous, 21-year-old Thao Bounlay raps three times on the glass door of a church near Paris, declaring to the parish his decision to be baptised.

data.title: North Korea to keep nuclear weapons 'forever': foreign minister
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea will keep its nuclear weapons "forever", its foreign minister vowed Thursday, dismissing the South Korean president's renewed calls for a denuclearised Korean Peninsula.

data.title: Thousands still missing a month after Nepal floods
data.description: KATHMANDU - The tsunami-like flood that cut a swathe of destruction through Nepal on August 26 has left the Himalayan nation grappling with heavy losses and mounting reconstruction needs.

data.title: 8 suicide attempts confirmed on US aircraft carrier
data.description: WASHINGTON - The Trump administration has acknowledged eight suicide attempts by US service members during the extended deployment of an aircraft carrier to the Middle East, a US lawmaker revealed on Wednesday.

data.title: Colombians in Santa Marta stay inside after violence wracks the city
data.description: SANTA MARTA (COLOMBIA) - Stores and schools closed and drivers mostly stayed off the roads Wednesday as the Colombian city of Santa Marta limped back to normal after a wave of drug-gang violence prompted a deployment of army troops.

data.title: Australian PM says OpenAI hacked government health website
data.description: SYDNEY - An autonomous OpenAI program infiltrated an Australian government health website in June in an "unacceptable" breach, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said.

data.title: North Korean IT contractor found remote work in New Zealand: agency
data.description: WELLINGTON - A North Korean IT worker used a fake identity to obtain remote work with a New Zealand company and then threatened to release sensitive information when exposed, Wellington's cybersecurity agency said Thursday.

data.title: Iran airlines cancel flights as US sanctions hit
data.description: TEHRAN - Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the United States tightened sanctions on Iran's aviation industry in a new effort to cripple its economy.

data.title: Morocco elects new parliament amid social frustration, youth discontent
data.description: RABAT - Moroccans worried about unemployment and inequality cast their ballots for a new parliament on Wednesday, in the country's first poll since a mass migration crisis and a youth-led protest movement highlighted widespread discontentment among young people.

data.title: At UN, OpenAI's Altman calls 'for extreme care' in AI
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - The current moment in AI development "calls for extreme care," OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told the UN Security Council on Wednesday, noting that the technology's advancement could accelerate rapidly.

data.title: US judge weighing Trump's White House ban on media outlets
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - A US federal judge was holding a hearing on Wednesday to consider a demand by CNN, MS NOW and Politico to have their White House access restored after their credentials were revoked by President Donald Trump.

data.title: Zelensky says Putin using fighters from 47 countries in Ukraine war
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin of using third-country fighters from 47 countries to prosecute Moscow's war against Ukraine.

data.title: Ditch ‘enemy state’ label, Japanese PM tells UN
data.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has called on the United Nations to scrap references to former Axis powers as “enemy states” in its Charter — a World War II-era designation that China and Russia have recently used to attack Tokyo.

data.title: Golan will remain Syrian, president vows at UN
data.description: UNITED NATIONS - Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa insisted at the United Nations on Wednesday that the Golan Heights region will remain Syrian after Colombia last month recognised Israeli sovereignty over the strategically important territory.

data.title: Rights groups press Malaysia to stop Rohingya returns
data.description: ​More than ⁠160 ⁠civil society organisations released a ​joint statement on Wednesday urging Malaysia to halt plans to deport ​Rohingya refugees to Myanmar, citing ‌severe risks of ongoing violence and forced conscription.

data.title: Russia probes bear attacks in region under ‘siege’
data.description: MOSCOW - At least six people have been killed in bear attacks in Russia’s vast Siberian region of Krasnoyarsk in a month, prosecutors said on Wednesday, as an official in a neighbouring region reported bears had put one town “under siege”.

data.title: ICC convicts Central Africa rebel leader
data.description: THE HAGUE - The International Criminal Court on Wednesday convicted a former Central African Republic rebel commander on four counts of crimes against humanity including torture and unlawful imprisonment.

data.title: New UK unit to combat disinformation from Russia, AI
data.description: LONDON - The UK will create an agency to fight disinformation coming from adversaries such as Russia and amplified by artificial intelligence, to help “separate fact from fiction”, Britain’s defence minister said Wednesday.
